title: Proof pages for a law practice
metaTitle: Law practice case study page: the decision
excerpt: A law practice case study page should show the constraint, the decision, and the kind of matter. Screenshots without a decision are decoration.
alt: A dim desk with an iMac showing a code editor beside a portfolio page, a second monitor with a mountain wallpaper, and a lit lamp, a place where proof is reviewed rather than decorated.
caption: A desk with the work on one screen and a portfolio on the other. Photograph via Unsplash.

faqs.question: What should a legal case study include?
faqs.answer: Include the constraint, the decision, and the kind of matter, in that order. Say what you chose to do and what you refused to do. End with how a similar client can request a consultation, including what they should send.

faqs.question: Can a law firm publish client results?
faqs.answer: Only when you have the right to do so, and only within the rules of the place you practice. Remove names and details that would identify a client. Do not write fake quotations. If a detail is necessary and identifying, leave the detail out or leave the page unpublished.

faqs.question: Are screenshots useful on a proof page?
faqs.answer: They are useful when they show the decision, such as a marked-up clause with identifiers removed. A photograph of a courthouse or a marble texture does not show how you worked. Caption the image with the point it is there to prove.

sources.title: How Long Do Users Stay on Web Pages?

markdown:
A law practice case study page should show the constraint, the decision, and the kind of matter you take. Screenshots without a decision are decoration. End on how a similar client can request a consultation. A person choosing counsel under time pressure is looking for evidence that you have handled a problem with a shape like theirs, and that you can say what you decided.

A shop can show the product. Hanabi's public work for Down the Cove can show a store after a migration because the store is public. A client file usually cannot be shown that way. The proof has to live in the constraint and the decision, told without the papers, the names, and the secrets. Google's helpful-content guidance asks you to show how something was done, including the evidence of the work, and it treats trust as the heart of experience and expertise on topics that affect someone's safety or finances. A law proof page is that kind of page.

## Constraint, decision, matter

Write those three in that order, near the top, in sentences a stranger can repeat.

The constraint is what limited the work. A lease that had to be signed in ten days. A letter that could not be ignored over a weekend. A company too small to want a courtroom. Two owners who still had to work together on Monday. The constraint is why the matter was hard. Without it, the result sounds easy and therefore unreal.

The decision is what you chose to do, and what you chose not to do. You marked up the guarantee and told the client to walk if it stayed. You answered the letter and refused to escalate. You split the work into a priced first phase because the rest could not be scoped. The decision is the proof that a person thought. A page that only says "successful outcome" hides the thinking the next client is trying to hire.

The matter is the kind, in the client's words. Shop lease. Termination letter. Founder dispute. Estate with a family business. That label is how the next client sorts themselves in. If the matter is one you no longer take, do not feature the page.

Keep each of those to a few sentences. Nielsen Norman Group's research is that people read only about a quarter of the text on pages they open, and they often leave within 10 to 20 seconds. The three facts have to survive that skim.

## What you can show when the file is private

Assume the matter is confidential unless you have a clear right to publish it. Then design the page around that limit, instead of stretching it.

Change or remove names, addresses, dollar figures that would identify someone, and the unique facts of a dispute. Say that you have done so. A reader should understand that the page is a pattern, not a dossier. If a detail is necessary to the decision and it would identify the client, drop the detail or drop the page.

Do not reconstruct a client's words. A quotation you wrote yourself is a fiction, and on a legal site it is a serious one. If a client has given written permission for a specific sentence, use that sentence and nothing around it that they did not approve. Most firms will have no such sentence. The page can still be strong.

What you can show is your own method. The questions you asked. The order you read the papers. The point at which you told the client to stop. The shape of the fee for that phase. Those are yours. They teach the next client what it is like to instruct you.

Check the rules where you practice before you mention a result, a court, or a client sector that is small enough to guess. When in doubt, describe the kind of matter and the decision, and leave the trophy out. A permitted, dull page is better than a vivid page you have to take down.

## Screenshots are evidence, or they are furniture

A screenshot earns its place when it shows the decision. A marked-up clause with the client's name removed. A one-page issues list with the dates removed. A diagram of the steps you actually followed. The image should make the decision easier to see.

A screenshot of your homepage, a marble texture, or a gavel on a desk shows nothing about the matter. The same is true of a full-bleed photograph of a courthouse you do not work in. The Princeton GEO paper, from Aggarwal and colleagues, reported that adding citations, quotations, and statistics raised source visibility, with their methods boosting visibility by more than 40 percent on the queries they tested. That finding is not permission to invent a number. A fake win rate is worse than no proof. If you have no countable result you are allowed to publish, do not borrow one.

Public work follows a different rule. An editorial site such as the Thomas Bewick project can show the real pages because the material is meant to be seen. Use that standard only when your matter is public. Do not treat a confidential file as if it were a storefront.

Write a caption that states the decision the image supports. "The guarantee clause, with the client identifiers removed, and the note that told them to refuse it." Alt text should describe the image. It should not be a string of practice-area keywords.

## How long the page should be

One matter, one decision. A page that tells three victories in a row teaches none of them. If you have three patterns you can publish, publish three pages and let each one end on the consultation.

A useful length is the length of the decision. Opening constraint. What you looked at. What you recommended. What the client still had to decide, because the decision was not only yours. What a similar client should send if they want the same kind of help.

Leave out the firm's history, the awards, and a general essay on the area of law. Those pages can exist. They are not this page. A client who wanted a textbook would not be on a consultation path. A client who wants to know if you are careful will read the decision and then look for the request.

Give the page one job in the navigation. Call it by the matter, not by the word case study, if your clients do not say that word. A tenant will look for lease stories or lease reviews. The internal name can stay in your notes.

Link to the service this proof supports, and to the person who did the work if they are still at the firm. If they have left, either update the page or archive it. Proof that points at a missing lawyer is a broken path.

## End on a consultation a similar client can request

The last section should be practical. If your matter looks like this, request a consultation. Send the document, the deadline, and the other party's name if a conflict check requires it.

Say what the consult will and will not do. You will tell them whether this kind of matter is one you take, and what the first phase looks like. You will not give a full opinion in the confirmation email. That matches the care the proof page just demonstrated. A page about careful decisions that ends with "Contact us for a free instant answer" undoes itself.

Repeat the boundary. If this proof was about tenant leases, say that you do not act for the landlord on that kind of lease, if that is true. The right client feels found. The wrong client is spared a wasted week.

Invite only the matter you can still do. A proof page for a kind of work you have retired is a trap, however proud you are of it. Move it off the navigation or mark it as a past pattern that you no longer offer.

## A simple test before you publish

Hand the draft to someone who does not know the file. Ask them to name the constraint, the decision, and the kind of matter. If they cannot, the page is still a mood piece. Ask them what they would send if their problem rhymed with this one. If they cannot, the ending is too soft.

Then ask a lawyer who was not on the matter whether anything identifies the client. Do this before the page is public. Taking a page down after a client recognizes themselves is a worse conversation than cutting a paragraph on Tuesday.

Read it once more for costume. Marble, Latin, and a stock scale do not make a decision more credible. Plain sentences do.

## Where this sits in the site

The proof page is not the menu. A client who believes the decision still has to find their way to the right job, and the labels have to match the words they already use. Read [how to set the navigation for a practice](/blog/navigation-for-a-law-practice) before you add a new proof page to a menu of department names.

When you want to talk through a proof page that is specific without exposing a client, [book an intro call with Hanabi](https://cal.com/hanabi/30min). Bring one matter you are allowed to describe, and the decision you actually made.
